Internships and Work-Studies.text: Hero academies use two kinds of field placement. Internships come first. After the U.A. Sports Festival, agencies that watched the broadcast send offers to the Hero Course students they want, and each student picks one; students without offers choose from a standing list of agencies that take interns every year. Before going, students choose the hero names they will use in the field. An internship lasts about a week. Interns follow patrols, office work and training, wear their costumes in public under their mentor's supervision and help in emergencies only at the mentor's direction. Without a license they have no right to fight villains on their own, and the mentor answers for their safety. Work-studies come later and require a provisional license. A work-study student joins an agency for a term or longer and works real cases between classes, with the academy's permission and under the agency's supervision. Work-study students carry more responsibility than interns, and the academy can pull a student from a placement if it judges the work unsafe or the student's studies suffer. Not every agency accepts students, and many prefer trainees who have already shown what they can do. For agencies, students are a scouting pipeline: a good intern or work-study student often returns after graduation as a sidekick.
